name: Stream and Wetland Restoration Grant (Tennessee)

funder.name: Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation (TDEC)

summary: Tennessee grants from natural resource damages recoveries for stream and wetland restoration projects, open to nonprofits and public bodies, with a 20% minimum match. The 2026 window has closed.

eligibility.rule: Keep the project within Tennessee near a targeted HUC 12 watershed
Do not use the project to meet regulatory requirements
Protect the project permanently through an easement or deed restriction
Have a project manager with demonstrated capacity to complete the project
Have capacity to administer, track, and report awarded funds
Be free of debarment, suspension, proposed debarment, and ineligibility

documents: Letters of commitment, for each partner listed

status.quote: The application opens on Monday, August 3, 2026. Submissions are due Wednesday, September 30, 2026.

opens.quote: The application opens on Monday, August 3, 2026.

applicant_types.quote: is available to nonprofit corporations, state agencies, federal agencies, and local governments.

geography.quote: be within the State of Tennessee in proximity to a HUC 12 watershed identified in the RFP

access.quote: please register and apply via the TDEC Online Grants System

window.quote: The application opens on Monday, August 3, 2026. Submissions are due Wednesday, September 30, 2026.

co_finance_required.quote: Projects are required to leverage additional resources to match the grant funding with a minimum of 20% of the total project cost.

effort.quote: Pre-proposal applications and supporting documentation must be submitted electronically via the TDEC Online Grants Management System at https://tdec.smartsimple.com/ no later than 4:00 p.m. EST on September 30, 2026.
A limited number of pre-proposal applicants will be invited to submit a full proposal to elaborate on their work for a second-stage review.

eligibility.quote: be within the State of Tennessee in proximity to a HUC 12 watershed identified in the RFP;
not be intended to help meet regulatory requirements;
Permanent protection through easements or deed restrictions are required.
have a project manager with demonstrated capacity to complete the project;
be performed by an organization with the demonstrated capacity to administer, track, and report the funds awarded.

the applicant certifies that he/she, along with any other officers, directors, owners, partners, employees, or agents, is (are) not presently debarred, suspended, proposed for debarment, or declared ineligible for an award by any State or Federal agency.

co_finance.quote: Projects are required to leverage additional resources to match the grant funding with a minimum of 20% of the total project cost. Higher matches will receive greater consideration for the value of grant funds requested. In-kind leverage is allowed and must be presented in the proposal budget.

after_award.quote: providing quarterly progress reports, monitoring baseline environmental conditions and project success, project outreach and communication updates, tracking and reporting in-kind contributions, submitting a final report
the Grantee must complete the TDEC Subrecipient Title VI training (accessible at https://tdec.tn.gov/title6/index.html)

documents.quote: All applicants are required to submit a pre-proposal, including the grant program pre-proposal application, project description, letters of commitment, budget, and budget justification. Applicants must also submit the Title VI Compliance Application Survey in the Grants Management System.
